ai.seo_question: What are the signs of moral decay and social inversion in the era described in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this passage from Nahj al-Balagha is often interpreted as a prophecy of the 'Era of Inversion' (Zaman al-Taqallub), reflecting the socio-political turmoil following the death of the Prophet and intensifying during the Umayyad period. It underscores the concept of *Taqwiyat al-Zahir* (strengthening the outward appearance) where political legitimacy is maintained through superficial piety while inner corruption prevails, a theme central to Shia critiques of early caliphates.
